problem: Validation success rate of Recurrent PREVALENT fluctuates drastically during VLN training, so the single final checkpoint may not reflect the model's potential performance.
motivation: The paper observes strong fluctuation in validation SR across training (Appendix B), meaning good intermediate snapshots are discarded. Combining several snapshots could exploit this diversity at low training cost.
key_idea: Save M snapshots during a single training run and ensemble up to k of them at inference via weighted voting on action prediction scores within beam search, plus a past-action-aware attention modification.
insight: Appendix D ablations show that increasing M from 5 to 10 gives SR 64.58 to 65.18, with saturation at 15 (65.3), and increasing k from 3 to 4 gives 65.18 to 65.56, with little further gain at k=5 (65.69). The case study shows the weighted voting lets one correct snapshot with a high prediction score override two wrong snapshots.
method: Recurrent PREVALENT base: uses candidate-action image features plus an all-zero stop feature, BERT instruction embeddings, and a cls token as the recurrent hidden state; features are projected into a common space for cross-attention.
Snapshot ensemble: saves M=10 snapshots during a single training run and ensembles a maximum of k=4 in beam search.
Weighted voting: combines member snapshots' prediction scores so a confident correct snapshot can override the majority.
Past-action-aware modification: regularizes attention between the cls token and instruction words, giving more concentrated and logically sensible attention (Appendix C).

setting.backbone: Recurrent PREVALENT (BERT-based, trained with IL+RL), snapshot ensemble
setting.training_data: R2R training data as in Recurrent PREVALENT (main text not available)
setting.observation: panoramic RGB view features (candidate viewpoint features)

numbers_note: Only the appendix is available; the main results tables and comparison against baselines are missing. The numbers are from the appendix ablations.
results: On R2R val-unseen the chosen snapshot ensemble (M=10, k=4) reaches SR 65.56 and SPL 59.2 (NE 3.75). Ablations show gains from more snapshots saturate around M=10 and k=4. The baseline single-model numbers are not in the provided text.
limitations: Ensembling k snapshots increases GPU memory (about 3,000 MB per extra snapshot) and inference cost
Only the Recurrent PREVALENT model is evaluated (as far as the appendix shows)
